rows.call: A gear curve as a game formula.
rows.decision: Approve it. A piece's budget is linear in the Level it is worn at and lives in data. Past tier 7 a band is a fixed step of the curve, and the step is one knob. It opens at the largest step that keeps the rider below, which is about +17% on the planned region edges (bands at Levels 110, 129, 151, 176, 206, 241, 282, 330 and 386). That is eight bands to Level 400, about one and a half a region. Every unique is a spend of its band at published rates. The two Luck numbers are keyed by Level with the same end points. rows.call: Collision (d): the log-scale kinks in the Level law at Level 100 and Level 300.
rows.decision: Drop the log-scale join. The law is the convex cut of the ruled table: hours a Level is one continuous line that never falls, and each ruled stretch adds up to exactly its ruled hours. A generator writes it from the table and nobody types a point. The ramp at Level 50 is the first piece of the same line, rising from what the four pays at 49 over about eight Levels. Nothing is smoothed by hand afterwards. The generator's rule is written here so the law is one line and not one of many: it is the non-falling line through every ruled total that has the smallest largest step between two Levels.
rows.reason: A Level should never get cheaper than the one before it, and a player should never hit a wall the day after a milestone. Patching two kinks by hand would leave the third one in.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED by my own script on the ruled table (2026-11-21). The log join makes a Level cheaper at three places, not two: Level 100 (11.0 hours, then 8.9), Level 300 (15.9, then 13.9) and Level 500 (23.1, then 23.0), and it jumps 29% in one Level at 400. The convex cut passes through every ruled point exactly (600, 1,680, 3,120, 4,580, 6,720, 13,440, 23,520 hours), has no cheaper Level anywhere to Level 1,000, and its largest step between two Levels is 8%. It reads 9.7 hours at Level 100, 12.8 at 200, 14.5 at 300 and 18.0 at 400. What stays is in the ruled table itself: Levels 200 to 400 cost almost the same (14.4 and 14.6 hours) and the cost then climbs to 21 hours after 400.

rows.depends: GR-6. Band P11 (no Level over twice the one before) and P12 read it. If Tyler wants Levels 300 to 400 to feel steeper than 200 to 300, that is a change to his table and not to the join.

rows.call: Skill at high Level, and endless ladders.
rows.decision: A hit stays skill plus gear and never becomes skill times gear. Skill keeps its late worth through rune tiers past 60, one every 15 skill levels at +10% each, and through the to-hit ratio. The Tower reads any floor from one row.

rows.call: The starting weapon.
rows.decision: The player picks a weapon for each hero at creation, from the six starter set rows. No card is preselected. Each card carries its measured tag from check C1 ("Good alone" or "Best in a party. Slow alone."). The hammer card carries a "Good first hero" mark. Heroes two to four come pre-filled as shield, staff and bow, one press accepts them and any pick can be changed. The pre-filled company always holds one healer, and the creation screen says so before a player changes it. The pick only sets what is in hand. Every hero still owns the whole practice kit, and skills never lock a hero to the pick. Core owns the row. Check C1 is still owed.
rows.reason: This is the first choice a player ever makes, so it should be theirs. But a brand-new player should not start alone on the one weapon I made slow on purpose, and should not have to know what a party needs.
rows.evidence: MEASURED (my C3 run, 2026-11-21): a start-kit four at Level 5 holds the Sewer on Normal with a shield in front (lowest health 84%) and with a hammer in front (77%), with no deaths in 128 hero-hours each. So a player who keeps the hammer hero in front is not punished.

rows.decision: The rested bank is cut. The Level table is the only clock, and a missed day is simply missed. The two old kill ladders are a separate matter: he said keep on the page, and keeping them as tracks on the one kill count is still a PROPOSAL he has not seen.

rows.wasBeforeSitting: Tyler said keep on the page 2026-11-21, and what follows is a PROPOSAL he has not seen. The rested bank stays and now pays. A hero banks the hunted hours it missed: every hour it stands at full stamina and is not hunting adds to its bank, up to 24 hours. Banked hours pay +50% Level XP on that many later hunted hours. So a missed day is half made up and a hero with a bank never out-earns one that hunted every hour. It is a way back and never a way ahead. The pace seat hunts all 12 hours, so its bank is empty and the Level law does not read it. It is one row of the XP chain and one number a hero, written when a hunt starts and ends, with no statement on the settle. The two old kill ladders stay as tracks on the one kill ladder: one kill count a monster a hero, the count the Bestiary stages and GR-78 already read, with the old rungs kept as rows on that count and no second counter. Sizes are a HYPOTHESIS.

rows.call: May a bought timed boost fill the Level XP cap? (the 11-04 avoid list against Crowns giving real advantages)
rows.decision: No. No Level XP boost is sold, for Crowns or for gold. The timed Level XP cap of +25% is filled only by the Hearthrise weekend.
rows.reason: Level is the score everybody is ranked on, and I put paid XP boosts on the avoid list myself. A kill speed boost is still a real edge you can feel, and it does not sell the scoreboard.
rows.evidence: COMPUTED: best gear 1.15 times a timed damage boost 1.10 is 1.27, against 1.58 with a bought XP boost (chapter 04). It also moves the date the next region must open from about day 37 to 42 to about day 53 (GR-6a).
rows.replaces: If Tyler says yes instead, it replaces the 11-04 avoid list line on paid XP boosts and the 11-18 line that power is never sold directly for Crowns.
rows.depends: MM-28, MM-29, MM-31 (the economy and MMO deciders, who may recommend yes). GR-6a works under either answer.
rows.was: TYLER CONFIRMS. Not decided here. My recommendation: no. Bought boosts fill the timed damage cap and nothing on Level XP. The timed Level XP cap of +25% is earned only, from events, world bosses and clans. A payer is then about 27% faster than a plain four through best gear and a damage boost, and anybody who plays the shared world can add the XP on top.
rows.fixNote: Core said no and content-economy said yes at about +15%. Tyler's words on 2026-11-04, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-21 all run Crowns to gold to an edge, and Level is the ranked score.

rows.decision: One system called Talents. A hero earns one talent point every five Levels, for ever. A point goes into a track. Every rank gives a small stat on a curve that flattens, and at set ranks a track unlocks a rule that changes how the hero plays its seat. A plan set once spends new points with no press. A reset costs gold. The first build holds five tracks (Force, Footing, Grit, Reserve, Linger) and the rank 3 unlocks. No number in it is decided.
